pr_body:
This commit adds tracing to the various places within raft where state transitions happen. When a message is first proposed, it matches the context of the original message to the raft entry and registers it for tracing. Then it adds to the trace at the key points during the transitions and finally stops tracing once a `MsgStorageApplyResp` is received past the entry.

Fixes: #104035

Release note: None

I cleaned up the PR and removed all the raft encoding changes. I left the tracing in place because it seems to be useful in a number of cases. I'm not 100% sure, but I think there is still a problem with the way I'm using tracing that is leaking.
@andrewbaptist Thanks, appreciate the commits separation. I'll review tomorrow.

@pav-kv Thanks for all the feedback! I implemented most of the changes and have a couple of TODO's in place. I also updated the test to actually validate the trace has the expected values (and removed the redundant test). 

There are a couple of minor outstanding points, but I'm not sure if they should be changed:
1) How to handle a proposal with multiple entries. I left it only tracing one, but its an option to change that (either now or in the future)
2) Different messages for different message types (with less fields). I've found it useful to have all the fields printed even if they aren't always relevant, but that could definitely be cleaned up later as well.

One very unfortunate thing I found with testing this morning is that there are a lot of "extra" traced messages such as from the queues such as this: 
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/master/pkg/kv/kvserver/replicate_queue.go#L748

Which means that we get a lot more traces in the log than we'd like during things like rebalancing and background jobs.

I'm tempted to move this to a different log file to avoid cluttering the main file, but I can also do that as a follow-on PR.

> @andrewbaptist
> 
> > I'm tempted to move this to a different log file to avoid cluttering the main file, but I can also do that as a follow-on PR.
> 
> Like to a separate `raft` logging channel? Sounds good if this isn't much work.

Unfortunately this was a bigger effort than I originally expected. Let me look at a few alternative options...

@pav-kv  - Some thoughts about the PR - I made a few updates last night based on your review.
* It would be good to at least get the protobuf changes in place before the branch cut. I debated adding a Term parameter to the protobuf, even if we don't use it for tracing. It might help if we later decide to use it. Thoughts? 
* I plan to add unit tests to RaftTracing directly rather than a system level test. Especially since the registration logic is a little more complex than before.
* The current approach disables the tracing by default. I'm going to run all the perturbation tests this morning with it enabled (plus https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/132713) and add some traces and real data to this issue. 

Any other thoughts on it?

issue_context.title: kvserver: add tracing through Raft
issue_context.body:
Currently, our tracing stops when we submit the proposal to Raft:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/da5be736ddb6579055b237b33c61024a3e4a0d70/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_proposal_buf.go#L906-L909

And only resumes once the proposal is applied locally:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/939f9552e8c5787506f589094888f52fca667175/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_application_decoder.go#L60-L61

It would be very useful to have trace events for the intermediate steps as well. In particular:

* Log append (on any replica).
* Submitted to send queue.
* Sent across the network.
* Received across the network.
* Submitted to the local Raft replica.
* Log read and/or entry cache read.

Because we control both the storage and network code, most of this can be done in CRDB code rather than etcd/raft, but we'll also need a couple of changes in upstream Raft. A rough sketch:

* A field on `raftpb.Entry` with arbitrary user metadata (in our case, the proposal ID from `ProposalData.idKey`).
* A mechanism to fetch the tracing context for a given proposal ID.
* A channel to propagate tracing information from and back to the caller, probably via `MsgApp` and `MsgAppResp`.

Jira issue: CRDB-28326
Epic: CRDB-37516
comments: In a past conversation with @tbg, he pointed out that there is already some infrastructure in place for propagating this and tracing through Raft, but I'm not familiar with the details. There will likely be some amount of research/archaeology to determine what infrastructure already exists.
Adding O-support, since missing Raft tracing regularly hampers diagnosis of latency escalations.

> there is already some infrastructure in place for propagating this and tracing through Raft, but I'm not familiar with the details

There are a [couple of fields](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/911f1ce389342459592d89fe7b78bcba3a2d265a/pkg/raft/raftpb/raft.proto#L104-L108) in raft messages:

- an arbitrary context, which some [flows](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/911f1ce389342459592d89fe7b78bcba3a2d265a/pkg/raft/raft.go#L999) use. Although we would have to be careful not to accidentally override it.
- a more recent addition is that requests can have an attached response, although these don't work across nodes.

Now that we've imported raft, we can modify the protocol more flexibly.

> A field on `raftpb.Entry` with arbitrary user metadata (in our case, the proposal ID from `ProposalData.idKey`).

An ideal ID would be `(term, index)` of the submitted entry. If it were that leaseholder==leader, we would get this ID at flushing to raft time, and use it to: a) watch the committed entries, b) tracing etc. Unfortunately, we don't have this information exposed to the proposer, so extending `raftpb.Entry` with a proposal ID might be the way in the short term.

_<WIP, I'm updating this comment with more details later>_

Here are some key points in the raft entry lifetime, between evaluation on the leaseholder and confirming the entry is applied to the state machine. We want most of these events traced.

["propose" phase on the leaseholder]
1. From the [proposals](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/021c72ae4a131bf511bff654fd3e4162947d3b15/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica.go#L739) map, they get [inserted](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/021c72ae4a131bf511bff654fd3e4162947d3b15/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_raft.go#L444) to the proposals [buffer](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/021c72ae4a131bf511bff654fd3e4162947d3b15/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica.go#L571-L584).
2. Later, the proposals buffer's `FlushLockedWithRaftGroup` builds the `raftpb.Entry` slices, and [steps](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/021c72ae4a131bf511bff654fd3e4162947d3b15/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_proposal_buf.go#L1038-L1042) them into `raft.RawNode` as a `MsgProp` message.
	- If the raft instance is not the leader, it may (if this feature is enabled) [forward](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/021c72ae4a131bf511bff654fd3e4162947d3b15/pkg/raft/raft.go#L1607-L1616) the proposal message to the leader over network.

["propose" phase on the leader]

3. The leader may drop proposals on the floor, but most of the time it [appends](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/021c72ae4a131bf511bff654fd3e4162947d3b15/pkg/raft/raft.go#L1268) them to its log.
4. Eventually, the leader [broadcasts](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/021c72ae4a131bf511bff654fd3e4162947d3b15/pkg/raft/raft.go#L658-L667) the `raftpb.Entry`-s to followers with a `MsgApp` message.
5. In parallel, it also sends the entry to the local log storage via `Ready` call (the protocol is the same as on the follower below).

["accept" phase on a follower]

6. The `MsgApp` message is stepped, and the follower [appends](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/021c72ae4a131bf511bff654fd3e4162947d3b15/pkg/raft/raft.go#L1661) the entry to the in-memory log.
    - It's possible that the follower's log is not up-to-date, in which case the below does not happen. Instead, there is a bit of back and forth with the leader until the log is caught up.
7. The entry is sent to local log storage via `Ready` call.
8. Once the storage confirmed storing the entry, the follower sends `MsgAppResp` to the leader.

["commit/apply" phase on the leader]

9. Once the leader collected a quorum of `MsgAppResp` covering an entry, the entry is committed.
10. The entry pops up via `Ready` call, in the `CommittedEntries` slice. Below the entry is applied to the state machine.
11. In parallel, the leader notifies the followers that the entry got committed.

["commit/apply" phase on the follower]

12. When the follower sees a commit index advancement, it returns newly committed entries via `Ready.CommittedEntries`.
13. The entries get applied to the state machine.

[on the leaseholder]

14. Once the leaseholder applied an entry that sits in the `proposals` map, it notifies the client.

----

Nuances:

- reproposals: there can be multiple `raftpb.Entry` submitted for a single proposal
- snapshots

A simple insert trace currently looks like:

![image](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/assets/39606633/1b5a82a9-69da-4e24-87d1-e66ba23cf226)


Or, with `vmodule=raft=1` to hit 

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/ceb19c5b75cf4aa02c68a669122349a3e9aca33d/pkg/kv/kvserver/raft.go#L258-L258

![image](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/assets/39606633/da1bc943-a082-4311-983f-2bdf3df94ab0)
Un-assigning myself as I'm not actively working on this issue.

Added

Isn't this just a poor man's implementationf of CAS (well it would be if you changed the if to a for). I don't think the normal uncontented CAS case is any more expensive than this. The race is so rare that I'm not sure its worth optimizing for.
Is `Context` never nil? Could you place a comment somewhere to this extent? Maybe in the `ProposalData.ctx` comment.
I added a comment to indicate that it is never nil and clean up the verbiage a little.
Should we also nil the `propSpan` here?
I don't think it was strictly necessary, but changed anyway to make it clear.
Could you also note that we can drop the trace here if someone outpaced us and incremented numRegisteredStore? And say that it's fine because it's a rare case.
Added

`Term`, `Index`, and `LogTerm` for this type of message are unused. Remove?

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/b2e1d9a00915b6e835893120ff029592755c48ae/pkg/raft/rawnode.go#L459-L465
Done

Do we want to hold the `t.mu` mutex while logging? Could do the data structure updates with `t.mu` locked, remember whether we want to log the message, and log it at the end after having released the mutex.
Updated. I'm not sure if it would have been a problem in practice, but I like the idea of minimizing the mutexes under lock.

So this is the one place where the context can change?

The thing is: we also modify `doneCh` above, for instance. I think the assumption is that all these fields are "owned" by the `raftMu`-protected critical section after some point (I'd have to page things in to figure it out, but [this](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/5531ba107658b49e922fe264ad23034a1317855a/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_proposal.go#L93-L102) comment seems relevant). So I wonder if we can assume the same thing for the `ctx` field. Is hiding it under an atomic needed?

There are also 2 places in `makeReproposal` and one in `evalAndPropose` that change the `ctx` of the original proposal. While the writes to this field are typically protected by the `raftMu` I don't think the reads were protected before and definitely are not after the changes I added. I only made this change after unit test failures that occurred without this. 

The `doneCh` is also modified, but in practice today all uses (read and writes) are already protected. I wonder if there is a different approach for some of these fields where they should be protected by a `proposalBuf.mu` or something to make this more clear.

I also added a TODO to track this down in the future. There is likely a lot more cleanup we should do in Raft logging once this is in place to wrap all the raft logging into the write context, but that is somewhat out of scope for this.
This is all resolved now that I'm able to use the propCtx directly after using `WithFollowsFrom`. So this isn't a problem anymore.

As an extra optimization. Could you check what mutexes are held in all stacks that update `r.numRegisteredReplica`? I have a suspicition that all of them might be holding `Replica.raftMu` or `Replica.mu`. If so, we could change the `Load()` to just read the local variable (but still update it atomically, for other readers).

If so, might add some `RaftMuLocked` / `ReplicaLocked` suffixes to methods that always hold a mutex, and optimize some atomics out.
I'd rather do this as a follow-up. I added a TODO to look at this. I wanted to look at some of this if we do a Raft retrospective as it was very difficult to know which locks are held whe.
Consider placing this check first. It is cheaper than fetching the context/span.
Swapped.
Done
Same thing: we flush lazily, so it's not always the fact that the limit is not exceeded.
Ack

One thing that's concerning here: it's possible that `MsgStorageApplyResp` never covers a registered index, or covers it much later in time.

For example:
1. The leader replicates a traced entry 100 to us, we register it.
2. Another leader is elected, and regresses the log to index 90. Effectively, it wipes this entry 100 from our log (as well as entries 91-99).
3. Only when the new leader proposes and commits all the way up to index 100 again, will we be able to unregister here. It's possible that it never happens, or happens much later, if there are no writes.

The approach with `LogMark`s would be more resilient to this kind of issue, because from the `LogMark` we can tell when such wipes happen. Before we fix the entry lifetime issues like this, I'm not sure it's safe to enable this tracing by default.

Or maybe it's fine if this index stays tracked longer time if it doesn't cause extra logging. A more concerning case would be if we're logging too much.

That is a valid risk. There are a few options to deal with it, but none of them are minor. 

1) Reintroduce the term and logmark. That's not great as I'm still not sure we conclusively know when to clear this entry. 
2) Reintroduce the term and close out all traces if the term on the replica ever changes. I'm not sure if we will miss some important traces
3) Allow the tracing to stay active. While it continues to use the concurrent limit, it doesn't cause too much logging.

With the change to set the default to 0 and the protection on duplicate MsgAppResp and MsgStorageAppendResp I think this should be safe enough. The worse case is that we will lose logging ability rather than having too many traces or log messages active. I could also consider adding a "max trace time" in the future to expire traces that have not moved in too long, but I'm not sure how important that is to do.

Slightly worried about the overhead here. We would be essentially calling `FlushAll` on every message. I realize this `== 0` check is what I previously suggested, sorry.

If we roll back to `if numRegistered > numAllowed { flush() }`, this would also be not ideal: if one or two ranges are not clearing themselves (e.g. it's quiesced or something, and observes no messages), then this check will also incur a flush on every message on all ranges.

Can we find a way to make the 0 case nearly free (not more than one or two atomic loads)? I'm pretty sure we need a variable local to this `RaftTracer` to achieve something like this.

I cleaned this up again. Now we have the two variables and check the "local" one first. We will only load the global one if we are likely to register. Also I think the overhead of reading a shared atomic should be ~ the cost of reading the setting. I ran some tests and I don't see it in perf traces.

Can there be inserts racing with this removal, and `RaftTracer` staying in a non-zero state afterwards?

I don't know if it's useful to log this case. If a replica is destroyed, maybe just silently zero it out. Or not clear/close at all, to avoid having to reason about this case. We're going to stop processing these messages anyway, and won't try to trace things.
Unfortunately with moving the numRegistered to a store level variable, it is important to clear these out. The case of adding during close is unfortunate. Maybe I'll add a
Could you please add a comment stating that this is optimized for the `numAllowed == 0` fast path? E.g. note that the `numAllowed == 0` case only costs us a couple of atomic loads per message.
Added
Alternatively, double-down on distributed trace collection if/when it's supported. So that the trace does not need to be plumbed back to the leaseholder / txn coordinator.
